diagnosis: I calibrated HBV with DDS on NSE over 1971–1997, starting the stores near their long-run levels (soil moisture 230 mm, lower store 480 mm). Daily NSE for the whole period is 0.876 (KGE 0.84, r 0.94, PBIAS +10%). I checked the same parameters on two halves without recalibrating, so this is a consistency check rather than independent validation: NSE was 0.859 for 1971–85 (+11% bias) and 0.908 for 1985–97 (+5% bias). The model overestimates volume, most in the early years. Observed flow grows over time relative to the model, which may come from effluent returns or abstraction changes; this non-stationarity is the main risk for 1998–2008. The fitted parameters describe a flashy clay catchment: soil store FC about 296 mm, BETA about 4.6, fast K0 and K1, routing MAXBAS about 3 days and a low upper threshold UZL of about 5 mm. The lower store drains very slowly (K2 about 0.0005 per day, at the bottom of its range), so it gives a nearly constant baseflow of about 0.25 mm/d and acts partly as a water sink. Summer low flows (observed minimum 0.06 mm/d) are therefore poorly shaped and probably overestimated. I tried a version with faster lower-store drainage (K2 at least 0.005), and it scored slightly lower. Snow matters little (1.7% of precipitation). The parameters that drive peak flows look well identified; K2 and the snow parameters do not.
